name: annual_mortality_rate_all_causes
confidence_reason: One primary study read in full, but from a declining Donana population in 1983 to 1989 with a wide interval (0.18 to 0.51); palomares2005 says mortality inside the national park is very low, so 0.37 likely overstates a protected population.
draft_note: Approved provisional assumption (AG, 2026-10-22):  low confidence does not block it.  Read in full 2026-10-25:  by status the rates were 0.12 and 0.21 (residents), 0.00 and 0.31 (young before dispersal), 0.86 and 0.70 (dispersers), so 0.37 is a mixture; ferreras2004 shows the same pattern.

name: female_home_range_km2
confidence_reason: The 10 km2 average comes from catsg, which names no study; the monograph (read in full) gives 9.5 km2 by the 100% polygon and 4.1 by the 90% polygon, so the estimator alone changes the value by about 2.3 times (9.5 / 4.1); the studies on food and range size disagree.
draft_note: The cross-parameter entries say that the effect of food on range size is disputed; run both versions (fixed range and food-dependent range).  palomares2001 (read in full) measured 9.5 km2 for adult females in Donana and found no link between rabbit density and range size, which disagrees with palomares2001a, another paper by the same author.  Its origin is not added here because the baseline table does not cite it yet (see the research-data pull request).

name: female_home_range_overlap_index
confidence_reason: Accepted manuscript read in full on 2026-10-25 (its supporting figures S1 to S3 and Table S1 are not in the file):  17 adult resident females in two Donana subpopulations, 1985 to 2008; median overlap 0.08 (range 0 to 0.57); contact between neighbouring females was extremely rare along the whole rabbit gradient, and extra food did not disrupt territoriality.
draft_note: Changed from low and not_checked after reading lopezbao2014 in full on 2026-10-25; Valerie chose none_identified and medium.  The monograph also found no link between rabbit density and range size.  The paper tests overlap, not range area, so it does not settle how food changes range size (see female_home_range_km2).

name: rabbit_density_spring_min_for_territorial_breeding
confidence_reason: Read in full (2026-10-25): 4.6 per hectare is, by our reading of the monograph's Fig. 13, a home-range average of spring 1996; the study says it was enough to support reproduction and could not determine how density affects breeding, so the rule that breeding stops below it is our assumption.
draft_note: The EU report reads the figure as a needed density; the primary source does not (it says it could not determine the minimum at which lynx fail).  Replaces the earlier pair with palomares2005, which is not a conflict:  both found no effect of density on reproduction in the range they saw.  palomares2001a (read in full 2026-10-25) gives the same two figures as a pellet conversion and does not call them minimums either.
